ei.title: When Not Selling Becomes the Best Sell

fullPassage:
When Not Selling Becomes the Best Sell

Have you ever come across an advertisement that actually encourages customers not to buy a product? It does not seem to make sense, but there are instances where companies have successfully used this somewhat odd approach. For example, there was a fast-food company that was concerned about public criticism on negative health effects due to the high fat content of fast food. Instead of trying to dispute the public criticism and claim their food was healthy, the company tried something different. They discouraged customers from eating fast food, like hamburgers, too often. Unexpectedly, this approach had an interesting effect. The company gained a positive image as being socially responsible, attracting more customers. This approach was also successful in the world of fashion. There was a rising concern about buying clothes and throwing them away quickly. This type of fast fashion trend has a destructive impact on the environment because excessive production of clothes produces a massive amount of waste. Surprisingly, one fashion company started to persuade people not to buy their clothes. They argued that people should consume less and far more slowly. This unconventional marketing strategy not only raised awareness about the harmful effects of fast fashion on the environment, but also increased the company's sales. People thought that this brand really cared about the environment, and they started to buy more of this company's products. To sum up, both of these companies positioned themselves as responsible brands by discouraging consumption, which ultimately captured the attention and appreciation of a growing audience.

questions.passage: Have you ever come across an advertisement that actually ①<u>encourages</u> customers not to buy a product? It does not seem to make sense, but there are instances ②<u>which</u> companies have successfully used this somewhat odd approach. For example, there was a fast-food company that was ③<u>concerned</u> about public criticism on negative health effects due to the high fat content of fast food. Instead of trying to ④<u>dispute</u> the public criticism and claim their food was healthy, the company tried something different.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 회사들이 이 접근법을 성공적으로 사용한 사례(instances where).
det.analysis: ✅ ①encourages: 3인칭 단수 현재형. ❌ ②which: 선행사 instances + 뒤에 완전한 절(companies have used) → 관계부사 where가 맞음. ✅ ③concerned: be concerned about ~을 걱정하다. ✅ ④dispute: try to + V(원형).
det.tip: instances where: ~하는 사례. 관계부사 where = 장소/상황의 선행사 + 완전한 절.

questions.passage: They ①<u>discouraged</u> customers from eating fast food, like hamburgers, too often. Unexpectedly, this approach had an ②<u>interested</u> effect. The company ③<u>gained</u> a positive image as being socially responsible, ④<u>attracting</u> more customers. This approach was also successful in the world of fashion.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 흥미로운(interesting) 효과가 있었다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①discouraged: discourage A from V-ing. ❌ ②interested: effect(사물)를 수식 → interesting(감정 유발 형용사)이 맞음. interested는 '흥미를 느끼는'으로 사람 수식. ✅ ③gained: 과거형 정상. ✅ ④attracting: 분사구문(결과).
det.tip: interesting(흥미를 유발하는, 사물) ↔ interested(흥미를 느끼는, 사람). -ing vs -ed 분사 형용사.

questions.passage: This unconventional marketing strategy not only ①<u>raised</u> awareness about the harmful effects of fast fashion on the environment, but also increased the company's sales. People thought that this brand really ②<u>cared</u> about the environment, and they started to buy more of this company's ③<u>products</u>. To sum up, both of these companies positioned ④<u>them</u> as responsible brands by discouraging consumption.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 두 회사가 스스로를(themselves) 책임감 있는 브랜드로 자리매김했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①raised: raise awareness = 인식을 높이다(타동사). ✅ ②cared: cared about = 관심을 가졌다. ✅ ③products: 복수형 정상. ❌ ④them: 주어(companies)와 목적어가 같으므로 재귀대명사 themselves가 필요. position oneself as = ~로 자리매김하다.
det.tip: 재귀대명사: 주어 = 목적어일 때 -self/-selves. positioned themselves as = 스스로를 ~로 자리매김했다.

questions.passage: This type of fast fashion trend has a destructive impact on the environment because ①<u>excessive</u> production of clothes ②<u>produces</u> a massive amount of waste. Surprisingly, one fashion company started to persuade people not to buy their clothes. They argued that people should ③<u>consume</u> less and far more ④<u>slow</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 훨씬 더 천천히(slowly) 소비해야 한다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①excessive: 형용사, production 수식. ✅ ②produces: 3인칭 단수(production). ✅ ③consume: should + V(원형). ❌ ④slow: 동사 consume을 수식 → 부사 slowly가 필요. far more slowly = 훨씬 더 천천히.
det.tip: 형용사 slow → 부사 slowly. 동사 수식은 부사. far more slowly = 훨씬 더 천천히.

questions.passage: Have you ever come across an advertisement that actually encourages customers not to buy a product? It does not seem to make sense, but there are instances where companies have successfully used this somewhat odd approach. For example, there was a fast-food company that was concerned about public criticism on negative health effects. Instead of trying to ①<u>dispute</u> the public criticism and claim their food was healthy, the company tried something different. They ②<u>encouraged</u> customers from eating fast food, like hamburgers, too often. Unexpectedly, this approach had an interesting effect. The company gained a ③<u>positive</u> image as being socially ④<u>responsible</u>, attracting more customers.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 고객들이 패스트푸드를 자주 먹지 않도록 만류했다(discouraged). encouraged(장려했다)는 부적절.
det.analysis: ✅ ①dispute: 원문 그대로. ❌ ②encouraged: 원문은 discouraged. 덜 먹도록 '만류'해야 하므로 '장려'는 반대. ✅ ③positive: 원문 그대로. ✅ ④responsible: 원문 그대로.
det.tip: discouraged(만류하다) ↔ encouraged(장려하다). discourage A from V-ing: A가 ~하지 않도록 만류하다.

questions.passage: This approach was also successful in the world of fashion. There was a rising concern about buying clothes and throwing them away quickly. This type of fast fashion trend has a ①<u>destructive</u> impact on the environment because excessive production of clothes produces a massive amount of waste. Surprisingly, one fashion company started to persuade people not to buy their clothes. This unconventional marketing strategy not only raised awareness about the harmful effects of fast fashion on the environment, but also ②<u>increased</u> the company's sales. People thought that this brand really ③<u>cared</u> about the environment, and they started to buy more of this company's products. To sum up, both of these companies positioned themselves as responsible brands by ④<u>promoting</u> consumption.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 소비를 억제(discouraging)함으로써 책임감 있는 브랜드로 자리매김. promoting(촉진)은 부적절.
det.analysis: ✅ ①destructive: 원문 그대로. ✅ ②increased: 원문 그대로. ✅ ③cared: 원문 그대로. ❌ ④promoting: 원문은 discouraging. 소비를 '억제'해야 하는데 '촉진'은 글의 핵심 논지에 반대.
det.tip: discouraging(억제하다) ↔ promoting(촉진하다). 글의 핵심: 소비 억제 → 브랜드 신뢰 → 매출 증가.

questions.passage: Have you ever come across an advertisement that actually encourages customers not to buy a product? It does not seem to make sense, but there are instances where companies have successfully used this somewhat odd approach. For example, there was a fast-food company that was concerned about public criticism on negative health effects due to the high fat content of fast food. Instead of trying to dispute the public criticism and claim their food was healthy, the company tried something different. They discouraged customers from eating fast food, like hamburgers, too often.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오: '패스트푸드 회사는 대중의 비판에 반박하려 했다.'

det.korean: 비판에 반박하는 대신에(instead of) 다른 것을 시도했다. F.
det.analysis: ❌ F: 'Instead of trying to dispute the public criticism' = 반박하려 하는 대신. 반박하지 않고 다른 접근법을 선택.
det.tip: instead of: ~하는 대신에. 반박을 시도하지 않고 다른 전략을 택함.

questions.passage: This approach was also successful in the world of fashion. There was a rising concern about buying clothes and throwing them away quickly. This type of fast fashion trend has a destructive impact on the environment because excessive production of clothes produces a massive amount of waste. Surprisingly, one fashion company started to persuade people not to buy their clothes. They argued that people should consume less and far more slowly.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오: '한 패션 회사가 사람들에게 자사 옷을 사지 말라고 설득하기 시작했다.'

det.korean: one fashion company started to persuade people not to buy their clothes. T.
det.analysis: ✅ T: 원문 그대로. 한 패션 회사가 사람들에게 자사 옷을 사지 말라고 설득 시작.
det.tip: persuade people not to buy: 사람들에게 사지 말라고 설득하다. 파격적 마케팅 전략.

questions.passage: This unconventional marketing strategy not only raised awareness about the harmful effects of fast fashion on the environment, but also increased the company's sales. People thought that this brand really cared about the environment, and they started to buy more of this company's products. To sum up, both of these companies positioned themselves as responsible brands by discouraging consumption, which ultimately captured the attention and appreciation of a growing audience.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오: '이 파격적 마케팅 전략은 회사 매출 감소를 초래했다.'

det.korean: 전략이 회사 매출을 증가시켰다(increased). 감소가 아님. F.
det.analysis: ❌ F: 'also increased the company's sales' = 매출 증가. 감소가 아니라 증가.
det.tip: increased(증가시켰다) ≠ decreased(감소시켰다). 역설적 결과가 글의 핵심.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 회사는 사회적으로 책임감 있다는 긍정적인 이미지를 얻었다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①positive: 긍정적인. 고객이 더 많이 몰려왔으므로 긍정적 이미지. ❌ ②negative(부정적인): 맥락 반대. ❌ ③neutral(중립적인): 매출 증가와 불일치. ❌ ④hostile(적대적인): 무관.
det.tip: positive image: 긍정적 이미지. 소비 억제 → 사회적 책임감 → 긍정적 이미지 → 고객 증가.

questions.passage: This type of fast fashion trend has a destructive impact on the environment because excessive production of clothes produces a massive amount of waste. questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 패스트 패션의 환경 유해 효과에 대한 인식을 높였다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③awareness: 인식, 자각. raised awareness = 인식을 높였다. ❌ ①revenue(수익): 맥락 불일치. ❌ ②controversy(논란): 뉘앙스 다름. ❌ ④suspicion(의심): 부정적, 맥락 불일치.
det.tip: raise awareness about: ~에 대한 인식을 높이다. 자주 출제되는 콜로케이션.

questions.stem: 위 글에서 패스트푸드 회사가 얻은 결과로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 사회적 책임감 있는 이미지를 얻어 고객이 늘었다

det.korean: 사회적으로 책임감 있는 이미지 → 고객 증가.
det.analysis: ✅ ④: gained a positive image as being socially responsible, attracting more customers. ❌ ①건강한 메뉴 개발: 언급 없음. ❌ ②광고 중단: 언급 없음. ❌ ③가격 인하: 언급 없음.
det.tip: socially responsible: 사회적으로 책임감 있는. 핵심 결과 = 긍정적 이미지 + 고객 증가.

ch: 패스트 패션은 환경에 파괴적인 영향을 미친다
패션 회사의 파격적 전략은 매출 감소를 초래했다
옷의 과잉 생산이 막대한 양의 쓰레기를 만든다
한 패션 회사는 사람들에게 덜 소비하라고 주장했다

det.korean: 전략은 매출을 증가(increased)시켰다. 감소가 아님.
det.analysis: ❌ ②: 원문은 'also increased the company's sales' = 매출 증가. 감소가 아님. ✅ ①③④: 원문과 일치.
det.tip: increased(증가시켰다) ≠ decreased(감소시켰다). 역설적 결과 = 핵심 포인트.

questions.stem: 위 글에서 원문과 다르게 바뀐 부분이 포함된 문장을 고르시오.

det.korean: 원문에서는 긍정적인(positive) 이미지, 사회적으로 책임감 있는(responsible)이라고 했다.
det.analysis: ❌ ③: 원문 'gained a positive image as being socially responsible' → 'negative image as being socially irresponsible'로 변경. ✅ ①②④: 원문 그대로.
det.tip: positive ↔ negative, responsible ↔ irresponsible. 핵심 메시지가 정반대로 바뀜.

det.korean: 부정적 건강 영향에 대한 대중의 비판.
det.analysis: criticism: 비판. public criticism = 대중의 비판. 뒤에서 dispute the public criticism으로 반복.
det.tip: criticism: 비판, 비평. public criticism = 여론의 비판.

det.tip: consumption: 소비. consume(소비하다)의 명사형. discouraging consumption = 소비 억제.
